summary_paragraph: A 55-year-old woman was admitted for recurrent nausea and vomiting, with a history of chronic gastroparesis, recent paraduodenal hernia repair, and multiple prior hospitalizations for similar symptoms. She presented with inability to tolerate oral intake, generalized abdominal pain with vomiting, and new-onset worsening back pain. Initial evaluation revealed leukocytosis, hypokalemia, and a non-obstructive bowel pattern. Imaging identified a new compression fracture in two mid-thoracic vertebrae. A post-pyloric Dobhoff tube was placed and enteral feeding initiated, which she tolerated well for two days before self-removing the tube and expressing readiness for discharge. Her nausea resolved, electrolytes normalized, and pain was controlled with medications. She was discharged home with improved symptoms, new prescriptions for antiemetics, potassium supplementation, and naproxen for back pain, and instructions to follow up with her gastroenterologist and primary care provider regarding long-term feeding options and osteoporosis management.
